evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Not asked. Joanna jumps straight into logistics ('Do you have any other furniture for office study garage balcony') after the customer says 'it's pretty straightforward move.'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: No concerns were raised by the customer in step 2, so this is n/a.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Rep does not address Value Days. Customer is on Friday 23 October. No mention of cheaper day alternatives or date flexibility.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Joanna says 'We don't take deposits at this time. The payment is only upon completion of the move' (rate lock / no deposit), then asks 'Do you have any questions or would you like for help for this move on that Friday?' (the ask, but not perfectly plain—it's bundled with a logistics question).
evidence_quotes.promises_delivered: Joanna delivers On-Time Guarantee ('if we're un late, we provide discounts for your move') and No Worries Damage Coverage ('No worries, damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage'), but no permission lead-in asking 'Can I share how we work...?' Both are delivered mid-pricing explanation rather than as a focused promise block with a close-the-loop check.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna gives a typical range: 'typically a one bedroom apartment usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours' and personalizes it: 'but for now I'll just call you more on the three to four hour mark' based on stairs and walking distance. Estimate given as '$58,088'.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details (furniture inventory, box count, walking distances at both ends, floor/stairs, room count) and confirmed all booking details cleanly including unit numbers, arrival window, and move date.
coaching_note: Start step 2 with the two-concerns question before any probing—'either movers not showing up on time or damage to items, are either of those a concern?'—to anchor the call on what matters to the customer, not the checklist.
